raw_case_text: A 68-year-old male presented with a 2.0x0.7 cm crusted keratotic plaque on his left infraorbital area that was concerning for nonmelanoma skin cancer. An H&E-stained section of a shave-biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation with pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and a few yeast with narrow-based budding suggestive of H. capsulatum. Urine testing for H. capsulatum antigen was negative. This lesion resolved within 2 weeks without medical intervention. Chest radiographs revealed small minimally calcified lymph nodes in the inferior right hilum and subcarinal chain (Fig. 1). One year later, the patient presented with recurrence of the lesion as a 2.0x1.0 cm thin, irritated, erythematous and crusted plaque (Fig. 2). No preceding trauma nor recent change in health status nor medications were reported. A full-skin examination demonstrated no similar lesions. Repeat biopsy was performed and showed findings similar to those previously described; however, numerous yeast forms were noted in this specimen (Fig. 3a, b). The organisms were highlighted by periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and Grocott-Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stains (Fig. 3c, d). Negative Fontana-Masson and mucicarmine stains excluded the presence of a Cryptococcus sp. Overall, the morphological appearance and the results of the special histological stains were consistent with those expected for H. capsulatum infection. Extensive microbiological testing, including Histoplasma H and M bands via immunodiffusion, urine Histoplasma antigen, Histoplasma mycelia complement fixation, Histoplasma yeast complement fixation, serum Blastomyces antigen and antibody, serum Aspergillus antibody, serum Coccidian antibody, and serum HIV antibodies and antigens were unrevealing. Cultivation of an aetiological agent was hampered by mishandling of the specimen prior to its receipt by the laboratory. A respiratory culture was not performed given significant delays in scheduling. Next-generation nucleic acid sequencing (NGS) of a 230 bp region of the internal transcribed spacer (ITS) that was amplified from the tissue block confirmed the presence of H. capsulatum. NGS was performed using an iSeq100 system (Illumina). Sequence data were analysed using an online database (ITS metagenomics app v. 1.1.0 at BaseSpace Sequence Hub). The patient was prescribed and started treatment with 200 mg itraconazole daily for a duration of 1 year and, to date, he has not reported recrudescence of the infection 8 months following his second biopsy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 68-year-old male presented with a recurrent 2.0 x 1.0 cm irritated, erythematous, crusted keratotic plaque on his left infraorbital cheek 1 year after spontaneous resolution of a biopsy-sampled lesion at the same site.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: One year prior to presentation, the patient underwent a shave biopsy of a 2.0 x 0.7 cm crusted keratotic plaque on his left infraorbital cheek (originally suspected to be nonmelanoma skin cancer), which showed granulomatous inflammation and rare narrow-based budding yeasts with negative urine Histoplasma antigen and resolved spontaneously within 2 weeks. One year later, the plaque recurred at the same site as a 2.0 x 1.0 cm irritated, erythematous, crusted plaque without antecedent trauma, health changes, or systemic symptoms.
subjective.past_medical_history: No recent change in health status or medications; no preceding facial trauma.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for a localized left infraorbital crusted facial plaque; negative for other skin lesions or systemic symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Cutaneous exam: solitary 2.0 x 1.0 cm thin, irritated, erythematous, and crusted keratotic plaque on the left infraorbital cheek; full-body skin exam showed no other lesions.
objective.routine_investigations: Microbiological & serological workup: negative urine Histoplasma antigen, Histoplasma immunodiffusion (H and M bands), Histoplasma mycelial and yeast complement fixation, serum Blastomyces Ag/Ab, Aspergillus Ab, Coccidioides Ab, and HIV Ag/Ab. Chest radiograph: small minimally calcified lymph nodes in the inferior right hilum and subcarinal chain.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial and repeat shave biopsies of left infraorbital plaque: granulomatous inflammation with pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and numerous narrow-based budding yeast forms highlighted on PAS and GMS stains (negative Fontana-Masson and mucicarmine stains excluding Cryptococcus). Next-generation sequencing (NGS; Illumina iSeq100) of a 230-bp ITS amplicon from the formalin-fixed tissue block: confirmed Histoplasma capsulatum.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Primary/localized recurrent cutaneous histoplasmosis of the left infraorbital cheek mimicking nonmelanoma skin cancer in an immunocompetent patient. Confirmation: Repeat skin biopsy PAS and GMS stains showing numerous narrow-based budding yeasts (Fontana-Masson and mucicarmine negative) and targeted internal transcribed spacer (ITS) next-generation sequencing (NGS) from the paraffin tissue block confirming Histoplasma capsulatum. Plan & clinical course: Treated with oral itraconazole 200 mg daily for 1 year, with complete clearance and no recurrence at 8-month follow-up.
